issues.legal_issue: An appellate officer appointed to hear appeals from public-premises eviction orders acts as a pre-existing civil court rather than as a persona designata.
material_facts: An appeal from an Estate Officer’s eviction order was heard by the Principal Judge of a City Civil Court acting as the appellate officer.
The governing provision designated the District Judge, or another judicial officer in the district selected by the District Judge, to hear the appeal.
The appellate officer was an existing judicial officer within the district judiciary, whose successor could continue proceedings and who exercised judicial authority in deciding the dispute.
issues.conclusion: The appellate officer under Section 9 of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 acts as a pre-existing judicial authority and civil court, not as a persona designata.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 designates the District Judge or another qualified judicial officer in the district to hear appeals; read with the Act’s scheme, including Sections 8 and 10, and the provisions establishing the district and city civil courts, it indicates that the appellate function is exercised by an existing court. The relevant tests include whether the authority is selected as an individual or as a member of a class or by virtue of office, whether it exercises judicial power, and whether it adjudicates a dispute judicially. The Court applied Thakur Das v. State of M.P., Mukri Gopalan v. Cheppilat Puthanpurayil Aboobacker, Central Talkies Ltd. v. Dwarka Prasad, Ram Chander Aggarwal v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Asnew Drums (P) Ltd. v. Maharashtra State Financial Corporation, Maharashtra State Financial Corporation v. Jaycee Drugs & Pharmaceuticals (P) Ltd., and the principles in Brajnandan Sinha v. Jyoti Narain and Virindar Kumar Satyawadi v. State of Punjab.

predicates.public_premises_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal from an order concerning eviction from public premises.
predicates.appellate_officer_is_preexisting_judicia: The appeal is heard by an existing judicial officer in the district judiciary.
predicates.appellate_officer_is_selected_by_office_: The appellate officer is identified by judicial office or as a qualified class of judicial officers, rather than selected as a named individual.
predicates.appeal_involves_judicial_adjudication: The appellate officer decides the parties’ dispute by exercising judicial authority.

issues.definition: When a public-premises appeal is decided through judicial adjudication by an existing judicial officer selected by office or class, the appellate officer acts as a civil court.

issues.legal_issue: An intra-court appeal is not maintainable when it challenges a single judge’s decision exercising supervisory jurisdiction over an order of a civil court.
material_facts: The respondents challenged an appellate officer’s decision in a writ petition invoking Articles 226 and 227.
The appellate officer was a civil court, and the Single Judge dismissed the challenge to that court’s order.
The nature and substance of the Single Judge’s decision showed that the jurisdiction exercised was supervisory jurisdiction, not jurisdiction to issue a writ under Article 226.
The respondents then brought a Letters Patent Appeal against the Single Judge’s decision.
issues.conclusion: The Letters Patent Appeal was not maintainable and should have been dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 226 and 227 confer distinct jurisdictions. A judicial order of a civil court is not amenable to a writ under Article 226; a challenge lies, where appropriate, under Article 227, and no intra-court appeal lies from a Single Judge’s decision exercising that supervisory jurisdiction. Whether the Single Judge acted under Article 226, Article 227, or both depends on the pleadings, the jurisdiction invoked, and the true nature and character of the decision and directions. The Court relied on Radhey Shyam v. Chhabi Nath, Ram Kishan Fauji v. State of Haryana, and Jogendrasinghji Vijaysinghji v. State of Gujarat.

rule.if: intra_court_appeal_proceeding and appeal_challenges_single_judge_decision and underlying_order_is_from_civil_court and single_judge_exercised_supervisory_jurisdiction

predicates.intra_court_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an intra-court appeal against a decision of a High Court Single Judge.
predicates.appeal_challenges_single_judge_decision: The appellant seeks review of the Single Judge’s decision by a High Court Division Bench.
predicates.underlying_order_is_from_civil_court: The order challenged before the Single Judge was made by a civil court.
predicates.single_judge_exercised_supervisory_juris: The substance of the Single Judge’s decision shows that the judge exercised supervisory jurisdiction over the civil court.

issues.definition: An intra-court appeal challenging a Single Judge’s supervisory decision on a civil-court order is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A Division Bench lacks jurisdiction to decide the merits of an intra-court appeal that is not maintainable.
material_facts: The Division Bench rejected the objection to maintainability and proceeded to decide the merits of the Letters Patent Appeal.
The appeal challenged a Single Judge’s decision whose substance was an exercise of supervisory jurisdiction over a civil court’s order.
The Supreme Court held that the Letters Patent Appeal was not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The Division Bench’s decision on the merits was without jurisdiction and could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: A Division Bench must determine whether an intra-court appeal is maintainable by examining the nature of the jurisdiction exercised by the Single Judge. If the challenged decision is an exercise of supervisory jurisdiction over a civil court’s order, no intra-court appeal lies; the Division Bench cannot then reach the merits. The Court applied Radhey Shyam v. Chhabi Nath, Ram Kishan Fauji v. State of Haryana, and Jogendrasinghji Vijaysinghji v. State of Gujarat.

predicates.intra_court_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an intra-court appeal against a decision of a High Court Single Judge.
predicates.division_bench_decides_merits: The Division Bench considers and rules on the substantive merits of the appeal.
predicates.single_judge_exercised_supervisory_juris: The Single Judge’s decision reviewed an order of a civil court in the exercise of supervisory jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a Division Bench decides the merits of an intra-court appeal from a Single Judge’s supervisory review of a civil court, that merits decision is without jurisdiction.
